html:
The Southern African Customs Union (SACU) links Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa. Set up in 1910, it is the oldest customs union in the world still in force.

It was born with the Union of South Africa. Britain ruled the three small territories of Bechuanaland, Basutoland and Swaziland, which were tied into South Africa's economy, and the union let goods move freely among them behind one common tariff. South Africa collected the duties and paid the others a share.

After the three became independent in the 1960s, the deal was renegotiated in 1969, and Namibia joined on its independence in 1990. A new agreement in 2002 gave the smaller members more say, and the headquarters moved to Windhoek. The shared customs money is a large part of the budgets of Lesotho and Eswatini. SACU now sits inside wider plans such as the African Continental Free Trade Area.
sum: The Southern African Customs Union (SACU) links Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia and South Africa. Set up in 1910, it is the oldest customs union in the world still in force.
